description: Exposure to contaminated water at U.S. Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune, North Carolina
eligibleLocations: Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune, North Carolina
Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) New River, North Carolina

presumptiveConditions.description: Cancer of blood-forming tissues, including bone marrow and lymphatic system

presumptiveConditions.condition: Aplastic Anemia and Other Myelodysplastic Syndromes
presumptiveConditions.description: Bone marrow doesn't make enough new blood cells
Cancer that begins in the cells of the liver
Cancer that originates in the lymphatic system
Progressive nervous system disorder affecting movement
Permanent kidney failure requiring dialysis or transplant
Cancer that begins in the lungs
Cancer that forms in the cells of the breasts
Inability to conceive after one year of unprotected intercourse
Buildup of fat in the liver

presumptiveConditions.note: For women who were exposed while pregnant or who conceived within 10 years of last exposure

presumptiveConditions.description: Changes in behavior, mood, or cognition
Autoimmune disease causing hardening and tightening of skin and connective tissues

evidenceRequirements.serviceConnection: Presumptive - Requires 30 cumulative days at Camp Lejeune between August 1, 1953 and December 31, 1987
evidenceRequirements.layEvidence: Not required for presumptive service connection
evidenceRequirements.serviceRecords: Orders or other documentation showing presence at Camp Lejeune

references: M21-1, Part IV, Subpart ii, Chapter 2, Section E

familyMembers.description: Family members who lived at Camp Lejeune during the contamination period may file claims under the Camp Lejeune Justice Act
familyMembers.legalAction: Separate from VA disability benefits - civil claims through Department of Justice

pactActExpansion.description: PACT Act added 10 additional presumptive conditions related to Camp Lejeune water contamination
